- Overestimate prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values.
- Underestimate prices in the late part of the forecast horizon; adjust upward for persistent upward trends.
- When the 30-day history shows a strong upward trend, model tends to overreact with a sharp spike followed by overcorrection; dampen the peak and smooth the decline.
- When the 30-day history shows a strong downward trend, model tends to underestimate and fail to capture the depth of the drop; increase the low end of the forecast.
- Model often overestimates the mean of the 30-day history, especially in the first 5–10 days; apply a downward bias to the first few forecast points.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overcorrects after sharp moves, leading to overshoots in the middle of the forecast; reduce mid-forecast values if the history shows volatility.
- When the true outcome shows a sustained upward trend, model tends to lag behind; increase forecast values gradually to match the trend.
- Model often fails to capture the true volatility in the last 5–10 days of the history; adjust forecast to reflect recent volatility patterns.
